question: A developer is writing a custom MCP tool that only queries data and never modifies anything. They want Claude to be able to call this tool alongside other non-modifying tools in parallel rather than one at a time. What should they do when defining the tool?
options: A) Set the readOnlyHint annotation to true on the tool definition
B) Set the idempotentHint annotation to true on the tool definition
C) Set the destructiveHint annotation to true on the tool definition
D) Increase the tool's timeout so parallel calls do not fail
correct_answers: A) Set the readOnlyHint annotation to true on the tool definition
explanations: Correct. readOnlyHint signals the tool does not modify its environment, which controls whether Claude can batch it for parallel execution with other read-only tools.
Incorrect. idempotentHint only indicates repeated calls have no additional effect; it is informational and does not control parallel batching.
Incorrect. destructiveHint signals the opposite behavior, that a tool may perform destructive updates, and does not enable parallel batching.
Incorrect. Timeout settings control how long a call may run, not whether Claude is permitted to batch calls in parallel.
